newsitem.title: INDIA: Peru's Fujimori says committed to aims of IMF plan.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Fujimori says committed to aims of IMF plan.

text.p: Peru is committed to an economic programme which is supported by the International Monetary Fund and will likely be reviewed by the Washington-based institution, President Alberto Fujimori said on Monday.

"It is not made by IMF, but it is our conviction," Fujimori told a news conference in the Indian capital, speaking on a proposed letter to the IMF outlining Peru's economic aims under a three-year loan programme.
German Suarez, the governor of Peru's Central Reserve Bank, said last week that the IMF was likely to review by early July Peru's forecasts of an improved set of indicators.
Peru would soon send the final draft of a provisional letter of intent that outlines its 1997 targets, Suarez said.
"This is very transparent in Peru. We publish every year the letter of intent," Fujimori said on the second day of a four-day visit to India.
He said the targets in the letter set forth Peru's own commitments while it receives support from the IMF.

The IMF has to approve these goals that form part of a programme that Peru is implementing in return for multilateral loans from the IMF, the World Bank and the Inter-American Development Bank (IADB).

The programme seeks to achieve 5.0 percent growth this year, up from 2.8 percent last year. It also aims to create sustained growth, control inflation and privatise most assets in the mining, oil, fishing industries.
The draft letter, published for public debate this month, said Peru seeks to cut inflation to between eight and 10 percent from 11.8 percent in 1996.
Fujimori said the reduction in inflation was a major achievement for Peru, where some years ago the annual inflation rate was as high as 7,600 percent.
